verdict.rationale: Rive documents its own programmatic surfaces for editor content. RML lets you create and modify Rive files as code with coding agents, an official MCP connection exposes editor tools, and a CLI lets an agent generate experiences. However, the MCP tools are explicitly only a 'first set' aimed at repetitive tasks, nothing claims full UI parity, and probes show no HTTP API or OpenAPI spec exists. Missing for 10: documented API/UI parity, a public versioned HTTP API with a machine-readable spec, coverage of editor actions beyond the initial MCP tool set, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: It lets you create and modify Rive content as code, making it possible to build Rive files with coding agents and other text-based workflows instead of working exclusively in the Editor.
The first set of tools are designed to let AI handle repetitive tasks, like creating complex View Models, State Machines with hundreds of states/layers, Layouts, Shapes, and more.
Build interactive UI, motion, and game experiences in the Editor, or let an agent generate them with the CLI.
